- It stickered around 40,000 in 2005 and a good one is worth about 00,000 now -- this car went UP more than four times. Never say it depreciated.
- Ford tried to buy Ferrari in 1963 and had a deal at roughly 18 million dollars, until Enzo read a clause that put Ford in charge of his racing budget and walked out of the room. Henry Ford the Second built the GT40 to beat him for it.
- It worked. Ferrari had won Le Mans six years running, and in 1966 the GT40 finished first, second and third, then won the next three years as well.
- 550 horsepower and 500 lb-ft from a supercharged 5.4-litre V8, through a six-speed manual, with the engine behind the driver.
- About 4,038 were built across two model years and then Ford stopped, and did not build another GT until 2017.

scenes.headline: Racing Legacy
scenes.narration: In 1966, the GT40 crushed Ferrari at Le Mans, taking the top three spots and reshaping racing history. This marked the start of a dominant era in racing.

scenes.headline: Aerodynamics
scenes.narration: The sweeping rear design and dual exhausts are part of what helps the Ford GT go from zero to sixty in just 3.3 seconds. Its aerodynamics are key for high-speed stability on the track.

scenes.headline: Driver-Focused

scenes.headline: Cooling Design

scenes.headline: Closing Question
scenes.narration: With a legacy of beating Ferrari and rising values, is the 2005 Ford GT the ultimate collector's car for you?

The sweeping rear design and dual exhausts are part of what helps the Ford GT go from zero to sixty in just 3.3 seconds. Its aerodynamics are key for high-speed stability on the track. A 5.4-liter supercharged V8 pumps out 550 horsepower and 500 lb-ft of torque, sitting right behind the driver. Its cockpit is all about the drive, with a 'rocket launcher' gearshift setup making it unmistakable. The prominent side air intake ensures the mid-engine powerhouse stays cool during performance highs. With a legacy of beating Ferrari and rising values, is the 2005 Ford GT the ultimate collector's car for you?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2005 Ford GT, finished in Midnight Blue Metallic with an Ebony interior, and will be displayed live at Willow Springs Reimagined as part of the Cars & Bids Willow Springs Collection. This Ford GT is owned by journalist and Cars & Bids founder Doug DeMuro, and associated videos are viewable below. This GT is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report and has reportedly been registered to two owners in California since new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this GT is a three-option car, equipped with the optional 18-inch front and 19-inch rear BBS forged wheels, painted brake calipers, and painted racing stripes. Additional notable factory equipment includes leather upholstery, carbon fiber seats, and air conditioning. Notable modifications reported by the seller include an SCT ECU tune, a smaller supercharger pulley, a Ford Racing exhaust, a Ford Racing short shifter, an Alpine head unit, and Ford GT designer Camilo Pardo's signature in the engine bay. Ford rekindled its rivalry with Ferrari when it rebooted the GT for 2005. Inspired by the Le Mans-winning GT40, the limited-production coupe represented America in the supercar segment with a heritage-laced design, a driver-focused interior, and a mid-mounted supercharged V8. Around 4,000 units were built, and Ford retired the GT nameplate until it launched the second-generation model for 2017. Power comes from a 5.4-liter supercharged V8, rated at 550 horsepower and 500 lb-ft of torque in stock form. Due to the modifications performed to this GT, it may produce more power, but a dyno sheet was not provided to confirm. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
